children.text: Under 28 days: neonatal team — use the AAP 2022 phototherapy and escalation thresholds.
Pallor, rapid heart rate or poor feeding: go to step 2 first.
Jaundiced after 2 weeks of age, breastfed or not: fractionate — total and direct (or conjugated) bilirubin.
Know your lab's method: direct-reacting and conjugated bilirubin are different tests with different cut-offs.
Never divide. Read the direct or conjugated value itself — the 20% rule misses biliary atresia.
Hemolyzed sample? It lowers the measured direct bilirubin. Redraw rather than reassure.

children.cond: Pale stools, or dark urine with bilirubin on dipstick — whatever the numbers

pill.text: Same-day pediatric hepatology: biliary atresia until proved otherwise — look at the stool yourself

children.cond: Direct > 1.0 mg/dL, or conjugated > 0.3 mg/dL — at any total

pill.text: Cholestasis, not this card: call pediatric hepatology today, to be seen this week — biliary atresia until proved otherwise

children.cond: Direct or conjugated normal, stools pigmented
Poor feeding, lethargy, high-pitched cry, arching or abnormal tone

pill.text: Emergency department now → NICU/PICU: possible bilirubin encephalopathy — emergency phototherapy, prepare for exchange; sepsis evaluation

children.cond: Any of: total at or near the AAP 2022 phototherapy threshold, whatever the cause (curves end at day 14 — use the day-14 value; expert opinion) · bilirubin:albumin molar ratio ≥ 1.0 · bilirubin rising day by day without hemolysis (Crigler–Najjar type I?)

pill.text: Admit: intensive phototherapy now; bilirubin and albumin; call hepatology today

children.text: Bilirubin:albumin molar ratio 1.0 ≈ total bilirubin (mg/dL) ÷ albumin (g/dL) of 8.8.

children.cond: Pallor, rapid heart rate, dark urine

pill.text: Emergency department now: acute hemolysis — CBC, reticulocytes, DAT, bilirubin

children.text: CBC with reticulocytes, blood film, direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test (DAT), blood group of mother and infant, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) activity (First contact).

pill.text: Immune hemolysis: hematology; follow hemoglobin — late anemia can need transfusion
Hematology: G6PD, spherocytes or other red-cell disorder on the film

children.text: G6PD deficiency plus a Gilbert-type UGT1A1 variant raises the risk of severe jaundice (Kaplan 1997).
Review the newborn screen: hypothyroidism, galactosemia, tyrosinemia (AAP 2022).

children.cond: High thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) or low free T4

pill.text: Endocrinology today: treat hypothyroidism; recheck bilirubin when euthyroid

children.cond: Poor weight gain or few stools
children.subtext: Assess feeding and intake; recheck weight and bilirubin within 1 week (expert opinion)

children.cond: Thriving breastfed infant, normal exam, pigmented stools; bilirubin well below the phototherapy threshold and not rising

pill.text: Likely breast-milk jaundice: continue breastfeeding; recheck total and direct bilirubin in 2–4 weeks (expert opinion)

children.text: Breast-milk jaundice can last for weeks. It is an unconjugated diagnosis: it explains nothing once direct bilirubin is raised.

children.cond: Formula-fed, or still jaundiced at 3 months (expert opinion), or bilirubin rising

pill.text: Hepatology clinic: repeat fractionated bilirubin; consider UGT1A1 sequencing (Crigler–Najjar type II)

children.text: Liver test norms for age: see Age-Based Liver Test Norms.
